name: Tanenhaus Spivey-Knowlton Eberhard & Sedivy (1995)
citation: Tanenhaus, M. K., Spivey-Knowlton, M. J., Eberhard, K. M., & Sedivy, J. C. (1995). Integration of visual and linguistic information in spoken language comprehension. Science, 268(5217), 1632-1634.
notes: The origin paper for the modern VWP. Real-object workspace + head-mounted tracker (put the apple on the towel ambiguity). Stimuli described in paper; no packaged set.

name: Allopenna Magnuson & Tanenhaus (1998)
citation: Allopenna, P. D., Magnuson, J. S., & Tanenhaus, M. K. (1998). Tracking the time course of spoken word recognition using eye movements: Evidence for continuous mapping models. Journal of Memory and Language, 38(4), 419-439.
notes: Foundational lexical-competition study (beaker/beetle/speaker/carriage). Item set described in paper; not packaged as a download. TRACE simulations widely reused.

name: Sedivy Tanenhaus Chambers & Carlson (1999)
citation: Sedivy, J. C., Tanenhaus, M. K., Chambers, C. G., & Carlson, G. N. (1999). Achieving incremental semantic interpretation through contextual representation. Cognition, 71(2), 109-147.
notes: Origin of the Referential Contrast Effect (tall glass with a contrasting short glass present). Adjective-driven anticipatory looks.

name: Altmann & Kamide (1999)
citation: Altmann, G. T. M., & Kamide, Y. (1999). Incremental interpretation at verbs: Restricting the domain of subsequent reference. Cognition, 73(3), 247-264.
notes: Classic anticipatory-looks study (the boy will eat the cake). Semi-realistic scenes rather than 4-object arrays.

name: Dahan Magnuson & Tanenhaus (2001) — frequency
citation: Dahan, D., Magnuson, J. S., & Tanenhaus, M. K. (2001). Time course of frequency effects in spoken-word recognition: Evidence from eye movements. Cognitive Psychology, 42(4), 317-367.
notes: Cohort competition modulated by lexical frequency (bench/bed/bell). Influential for frequency effects in lexical access.

name: Dahan Magnuson Tanenhaus & Hogan (2001) — subcategorical
citation: Dahan, D., Magnuson, J. S., Tanenhaus, M. K., & Hogan, E. M. (2001). Subcategorical mismatches and the time course of lexical access: Evidence for lexical competition. Language and Cognitive Processes, 16(5-6), 507-534.
notes: Cross-spliced coarticulatory mismatch; fine-grained phonetic detail. Stimuli described in paper.

name: Huettig & Altmann (2005) — semantic
citation: Huettig, F., & Altmann, G. T. M. (2005). Word meaning and the control of eye fixation: Semantic competitor effects and the visual world paradigm. Cognition, 96(1), B23-B32.
notes: Semantic-category competitor (hear piano, look at trumpet). 30 scenes. Feature-norm similarity correlated with fixations.

name: Huettig & McQueen (2007) — phon/sem/shape
citation: Huettig, F., & McQueen, J. M. (2007). The tug of war between phonological, semantic and shape information in language-mediated visual search. Journal of Memory and Language, 57(4), 460-482.
notes: Dissociates phonological vs semantic vs visual-shape competitors and their timing. Dutch materials.

name: BOSS — Bank of Standardized Stimuli
citation: Brodeur, M. B., Dionne-Dostie, E., Montreuil, T., & Lepage, M. (2010). The Bank of Standardized Stimuli (BOSS), a new set of 480 normative photos of objects. PLoS ONE, 5(5), e10773.
notes: Not VWP-specific but the most common normed object-photo source for building VWP displays. Used in the OpenSesame VWP tutorial. Name agreement / familiarity norms included.

name: MultiPic
citation: Duñabeitia, J. A., Crepaldi, D., Meyer, A. S., New, B., Pliatsikas, C., Smolka, E., & Brysbaert, M. (2018). MultiPic: A standardized set of 750 drawings with norms for six European languages. Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology, 71(4), 808-816.
language: multilingual (EN, ES, FR, DE, IT, NL)
notes: 750 colored drawings normed for naming across six languages. Useful for cross-linguistic VWP display construction. Note non-commercial license.

name: Rossion & Pourtois (2004) colorized Snodgrass-Vanderwart
citation: Rossion, B., & Pourtois, G. (2004). Revisiting Snodgrass and Vanderwart's object pictorial set: The role of surface detail in basic-level object recognition. Perception, 33(2), 217-236.
notes: Colorized/textured version of the classic Snodgrass & Vanderwart (1980) 260-item set. Common VWP display source.

name: OpenSesame VWP Tutorial Project
citation: Mathôt, S., Schreij, D., & Theeuwes, J. (2012). OpenSesame: An open-source, graphical experiment builder for the social sciences. Behavior Research Methods, 44(2), 314-324.
notes: Complete runnable VWP experiment + stimuli built for teaching. Good template for experiment structure and timing.

name: Referential Contrast Effect (VWP eye-tracking) — OSF
citation: OSF project (2022). Referential contrast effect: Visual World paradigm with eye-tracking.
notes: Study repository including eye-tracking data, in the Sedivy referential-contrast tradition. CONTENTS UNVERIFIED — confirm stimuli/license before reuse.

name: Eye-movement Suppression in the VWP — OSF
citation: Eye-movement suppression in the visual world paradigm. Open Mind, 8, 1012-1036 (2024).
notes: Data + analysis scripts (doi:10.1162/opmi_a_00157). Methods-focused; useful for analysis pipelines more than for stimuli. CONTENTS UNVERIFIED.
